concurrentContractCaveat.detail: negative_stop checks owns_claim separately from runtime_epoch CAS, ignores CAS failure and unconditionally writes global readiness/stopping flags afterwards. A concurrent old-reservation call which passed the early check can therefore write false/true after physical_returned releases claim and a new reservation activates. A successful old-epoch CAS can also pause before those flag stores, so merely returning on CAS failure is insufficient.
constructibleAtPrivateMethodBoundary: ThreadB old.physical_returned releases claim then new.reserve_runtime/new.activate sets fresh epoch and ready=true.
ThreadA epoch update rejects the fresh epoch but late global runtime_ready=false store makes runtime_generation None.
Alternate: ThreadA succeeds old epoch update and pauses before flag stores; ThreadB returns/reserves/activates, then same late flag write follows.
actualCallerReachabilityAudit: Whole fc-bootstrap rg shows production physical_returned only called in RuntimeOwner::poll(&mut self), after original HTTP thread physical exit.
Public request_stop_at(&self) cannot safely race poll(&mut self) on the same RuntimeOwner using ordinary Rust borrowing.
HTTP-thread negative_stop occurs before that thread exits, so original production poll cannot concurrently release this claim while that call runs.
No current public/UI path reaching the private-boundary schedule has been established; do not promote it to an observed or proven productP1.
concurrentContractCaveat.recommendation: If exact reservation methods are intended thread-safe independently, bind readiness/stopping to the exact monotonic epoch or serialize the entire check/write/physical-return/new-reserve transition with bounded metadata coordination. Preserve atomic nonwaiting negative admission and do not introduce IO/worker/ledger waits. Otherwise document and enforce the stronger call-site ordering contract and test it.
